chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn (or another) from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Malik ibn Atiyyah from Abd al-A'la ibn A'yan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who caught game in the open land (al-Hill), tied it up to the side of the Sanctuary (al-Haram), and the game walked with its tether until it entered the Sanctuary with the tether around its neck. The man pulled it with its rope until he brought it out, while the man himself remained in the open land outside the Sanctuary. He said: 'Its price and its meat are forbidden, like the carcass (of a dead animal).'

And whoever kills game while he is in a state of Ihram (or permitted) in the area between him and the Sanctuary, within the distance of a Bair (a stage of travel), the redemption (Fida') is incumbent upon him. He narrated.

key_terms.الرِّبَاطُ: Tether or rope used to tie the animal
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (specifically Mecca/Medina), a sacred area with specific hunting restrictions
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: The open land outside the Sanctuary boundaries
key_terms.الْفِدَاءُ: Redemption or compensation (usually in the form of food or animals) for breaking Ihram or hunting
key_terms.بَرِيدٌ: A distance measurement, roughly a stage of travel (approx. 48 km)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on game caught in the open land that enters the Sanctuary while tethered?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between hunting within the sanctuary versus the open land, establishing that tethered game pulled into the Haram while the hunter remains in the Hill renders the meat and price Haram, akin to the carcass of a dead animal. It further codifies the *Fida'* (redemption) liability for those who kill game within a *Bair* (approx. 3-4 miles) of the boundary, reflecting the juristic precision of the Imams in defining spatial limits of sanctity.
